key_findings: Reasoning budget has a real effect on generation: tokens increase from 265 to 402 as budget goes 256->1024
Additional reasoning does NOT improve policy accuracy; it degrades it (65% -> 25%)
Budgets 512+ are truncated even at max_tokens=2048 because reasoning consumes the token budget before the JSON answer is produced
The model's fundamental weakness is DEFER (0% accuracy) — it confuses DEFER with STOP or FAIL_CLOSED
RETRIEVE accuracy (67%) is close but below the 75% gate
Per-request thinking_budget_tokens works on llama.cpp, enabling single-server multi-budget testing
The --reasoning-format deepseek mode captures reasoning_content separately from the JSON answer
scientific_interpretation: LFM2.5-2.6B cannot reliably distinguish DEFER from STOP, nor consistently choose RETRIEVE when retrieval is the correct affordance. The controller interface (7-action vocabulary, JSON schema, frozen policy states) is not the bottleneck — model capacity is. Additional reasoning budget does not compensate; it introduces truncation without improving action selection.
